grammarFocus: 第一、第二条件句的常见用途；建议与可能性的表达。
title: The Lantern Lane Repair Café
instructions: 阅读下面的文章，回答10个问题。文章是关于一个社区维修咖啡馆的模拟教育材料，不是真实事件。请根据文章内容选择正确答案或填空。填空题答案必须来自原文，且不超过字数限制。判断题请选择 True、False 或 Not Given。
passage:
Lantern Lane is a quiet street in an old part of town. Most of the houses were built over eighty years ago, and many of the people who live there have been neighbours for a long time. Last autumn, the local council announced a new plan. They wanted to reduce waste in the area. The plan said that every household should throw away less and repair more. At first, many residents did not know what to do. They had broken lamps, old radios, and chairs with loose legs, but they did not have the skills to fix them.

A woman named Mrs. Chen lived on Lantern Lane. She had worked as an electrician for thirty years before she retired. She read the council's plan and thought, "If we start a repair café, people can bring their broken things and we can fix them together." She talked to her neighbour, Mr. Patel, who was a carpenter. He agreed immediately. "If you find a place," he said, "I will bring my tools." Mrs. Chen asked the council for permission to use the small community hall at the end of the street. The council said yes, but only on Saturday mornings.

The first repair café opened in November. About fifteen people came. They brought a lamp, two radios, a wooden chair, and a broken toy train. Mrs. Chen and Mr. Patel fixed most of the items. Some things could not be repaired, but the owners learned why. One young man, named Leo, brought a small fan that did not work. Mrs. Chen showed him how to test the wires. "If you check the fuse first," she said, "you will often find the problem." Leo was surprised. He said, "I didn't know it was so simple." He stayed for the whole morning and helped other people.

By January, the repair café had become popular. More than forty people came each Saturday. The hall was often full. Some volunteers suggested opening a second café on Sunday, but Mrs. Chen disagreed. "If we open on Sunday," she said, "we will not have enough volunteers. We might make mistakes." The group decided to stay with Saturday mornings. They also started a small noticeboard where people could write down what they needed. One note said, "I need help with a sewing machine." Another said, "I can teach basic bicycle repair." The noticeboard helped people share skills.

However, there was a problem with money. The council gave the group a small grant, but it was not enough to buy new tools. Mr. Patel suggested asking local shops for help. "If we explain our project to the shops," he said, "they might donate old tools or materials." The group wrote a short letter and visited five shops. Three shops agreed to help. A hardware shop gave them a box of screws and some wire. A bicycle shop donated old inner tubes. A furniture shop gave them wood offcuts. With these donations, the repair café could fix more things.

In March, the council asked Mrs. Chen to speak at a town meeting. They wanted other neighbourhoods to learn from Lantern Lane. Mrs. Chen said, "If you want to start a repair café, you should begin with a small group. You do not need much money. You need people who are willing to teach and people who are willing to learn." She also said, "If we had not worked together, none of this would have happened." The council was impressed and promised to share the Lantern Lane guide with other areas.

Today, the repair café is still running. It has fixed more than two hundred items. Mrs. Chen says the best part is not the repairs. "People talk to each other here," she says. "If you fix a lamp with your neighbour, you become friends." The group now has a waiting list for volunteers. They advise other communities: "Start small, listen to everyone, and do not be afraid to ask for help."

questions.prompt: Why did the council announce a new plan last autumn?
options: To reduce waste in the area.
answers: To reduce waste in the area.
questions.explanation: 文章第一段提到 'They wanted to reduce waste in the area.'，因此答案是减少浪费。
questions.evidence: They wanted to reduce waste in the area.

questions.prompt: What was Mrs. Chen's job before she retired?
questions.explanation: 第二段提到 'She had worked as an electrician for thirty years before she retired.'，所以她是电工。
questions.evidence: She had worked as an electrician for thirty years before she retired.

questions.prompt: What did Mr. Patel do for a living? (Use one word from the passage)
questions.explanation: 第二段提到 'Mr. Patel, who was a carpenter'，因此他的职业是木匠。
questions.evidence: Mr. Patel, who was a carpenter

questions.prompt: When did the first repair café open?
questions.explanation: 第三段开头提到 'The first repair café opened in November.'，所以是十一月。
questions.evidence: The first repair café opened in November.

questions.prompt: Why did Mrs. Chen disagree with opening a second café on Sunday?
options: She thought there would not be enough volunteers.
She thought Sunday was a busy day for shops.
She thought the hall was too small.
She thought the council would not allow it.
answers: She thought there would not be enough volunteers.
questions.explanation: 第四段中 Mrs. Chen 说 'If we open on Sunday, we will not have enough volunteers.'，因此她担心志愿者不够。
questions.evidence: If we open on Sunday, we will not have enough volunteers.

questions.prompt: What did the hardware shop give to the repair café?
options: A box of screws and some wire.
answers: A box of screws and some wire.
questions.explanation: 第五段提到 'A hardware shop gave them a box of screws and some wire.'，所以五金店给了螺丝和电线。
questions.evidence: A hardware shop gave them a box of screws and some wire.

questions.prompt: What did the council ask Mrs. Chen to do in March?
options: To speak at a town meeting.
To write a guide for other areas.
To open a second repair café.
To teach a class at the community hall.
answers: To speak at a town meeting.
questions.explanation: 第六段提到 'In March, the council asked Mrs. Chen to speak at a town meeting.'，因此是去镇会议上发言。
questions.evidence: In March, the council asked Mrs. Chen to speak at a town meeting.

questions.prompt: How many items has the repair café fixed so far?
questions.explanation: 最后一段提到 'It has fixed more than two hundred items.'，所以是两百多件。
questions.evidence: It has fixed more than two hundred items.

questions.prompt: The council gave the repair café enough money to buy new tools.
questions.explanation: 第五段提到 'The council gave the group a small grant, but it was not enough to buy new tools.'，与题目陈述相反，因此是 False。
questions.evidence: The council gave the group a small grant, but it was not enough to buy new tools.

questions.prompt: The repair café has a waiting list for volunteers.
questions.explanation: 最后一段提到 'The group now has a waiting list for volunteers.'，因此是 True。
questions.evidence: The group now has a waiting list for volunteers.

grammar.title: 第一、第二条件句的常见用途；建议与可能性的表达
grammar.explanation: 第一条件句表示可能发生的情况及其结果，结构为 if + 一般现在时，主句用 will/can/may + 动词原形。第二条件句表示假设或不太可能的情况，结构为 if + 一般过去时，主句用 would/could/might + 动词原形。建议可以用 'suggest + 动名词' 或 'suggest that + 主语 + (should) + 动词原形'，可能性可以用 may/might/could 表达。
grammar.example: If you close the park, the children will have nowhere to play.

questions.prompt: If it rains tomorrow, we ______ the garden project.
questions.explanation: 第一条件句表示将来可能发生的情况，主句用 will + 动词原形。

questions.prompt: If I were you, I ______ to the council meeting.
questions.explanation: 第二条件句表示假设，if 从句用过去时 (were)，主句用 would + 动词原形。

questions.prompt: The committee suggested ______ a fence around the garden.
questions.explanation: suggest 后接动名词形式，表示建议做某事。

questions.prompt: The teenagers ______ come to the garden if they have nothing else to do.
questions.explanation: might 表示可能性，这里表示 teenagers 可能来花园。
